newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber bounces back, ends up on buying.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber bounces back, ends up on buying.

text.p: Rubber futures finished the week higher on Friday, recovering from a one-day lull as healthy shortcovering shored up gains in the market, dealers said.

"The local boys did some shortcovering. The volume was not bad, especially for RSS3 and to a certain extent RSS1 rubber. Volume for TSR20 rubber, though, remained modest," a rubber trader in a foreign commodity house said.

The trade snapped to life in the afternoon session as buying for prompt delivery lifted the market. The local exchange was helped along by firmer Tokyo prices. Tokyo's benchmark August contract gained 1.2 yen to end at 150.2.
"It's hard to tell if the sentiment will spill over into next week. It will again be a wait-and-see game," a dealer said.
Total volume traded for RSS3 rubber reached a week-high of around 10,900 tonnes with volume for RSS1 rubber at about 2,900 tonnes, dealers said.

At around 0945 GMT, April RSS3 was seen at 121.50-123.50 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 121.50 cents. April RSS1 was seen at 173.00-175.00 Singapore cents (US$1.22-$1.23) a kg from the previous 172.50 cents. April TSR20 was seen at 168.50-170.50 Singapore cents (US$1.18-$1.20) a kg from yesterday's 168.25 cents. -- (US$1-S$1.42) - Rene Pastor (65-870-3305)
